document.slice: P1A.3b — grounded text generation and durable outbound delivery

priorDeployment.migration118: Applied, reported by user on 2026-11-03; no independent production verification.
priorDeployment.liveChannel: No production configuration or message delivery inspected.

implemented: Company → WhatsApp → Configure Sophia replies selects a published tenant agent release and Draft for review or Automatic text replies. Settings use optimistic revisions.
Existing approved instruction revisions, agent release manifests, published knowledge snapshots and capability grants are reused; no separate FAQ store.

Background generation retrieves at most five bounded approved source excerpts, uses the existing provider-neutral reasoning port with no tools or private staff notes, requires cited snapshot IDs and routes missing/unsupported results to the team.
Generation is pinned to both agent release and response-binding revision; citations, source publication/grants and provider eligibility are rechecked after generation and before automated dispatch.

Draft review, customer text composer, separate internal notes, explicit Resume Sophia and pending-work polling. Failed submissions retain text and the retry key; drafts never silently replace typed text.

Automatic text enquiries use bot ownership only when enabled. Existing paused/human threads remain with the team until explicitly resumed. Voice/media enquiries remain a human-review placeholder in this phase.

Durable idempotent outbox, bounded send worker, current handler/authority checks, opt-out, closed-lead and customer reply-window enforcement. Ownership changes, new messages and response-policy changes cancel undispatched work.

Official Cloud API text adapter includes an opaque outbox correlation ID. Accepted messages enter the timeline once; delivery/read statuses reconcile monotonically, including status-before-response races.

Timeouts, malformed success, ambiguous upstream errors and expired dispatch leases become Delivery uncertain and are not automatically resent. Only explicit rate-limit rejections use bounded delayed retries.
Delayed old inbound messages remain in history without replacing the current question or invalidating its answer.

schema.protection: FORCE tenant RLS, explicit least-privilege grants, tenant/conversation/source foreign keys, published release tenant FK, ownership-version cancellation trigger, bounded usage/source JSON and indexed queue/detail reads.

api.humanReply: POST /api/bm/lead-assistant/leads/:leadId/replies with UUID requestKey, expected ownership version and body
api.resume: Existing ownership endpoint accepts bot only after current tenant, handler, agent/provider, opt-out and window checks
api.detail: Existing authorized lead detail adds reply eligibility, latest five jobs and ten outgoing states; no email/phone fields added to register rows.

authorization.company: Existing active organisation_owner or chief_executive authority controls bindings. Neither browser tenant IDs nor provider/model choices are trusted.
authorization.lead: Assigned advisors and authorized enquiry/fallback owners use the existing inbox scope. Human send requires the current handler; dispatch revalidates current active staff and role/assignment.
authorization.reasoning: A deployed reasoning adapter/credential reference must match a published reasoning provider binding in an enabled, published experience included in the pinned tenant agent release and business profile. This slice supports the existing environment-backed adapters with empty provider settings; custom per-profile settings/credentials are rejected rather than ignored.
authorization.knowledge: Only pinned revision IDs with current published/ready/active source state and enabled capability grants within the release business profile are retrieved. Draft, retired, revoked and cross-tenant records cannot supply automated replies.

configuration.profileNotes: Extend the existing WHATSAPP_INBOUND_PROFILES entry; example version is illustrative, not a claim about the latest supported Graph version. Pin a supported version during actual setup. Store the token only in the deployment secret store. App secret, verify token, customer/WABA/phone IDs stay as configured for receiving.
configuration.reasoningNotes: Use the existing Runtime server-side provider credentials/models and their approved published configuration. No credentials or models are entered in the browser. The server allowlist and published experience binding must agree.

flags.WHATSAPP_REPLY_WORKER_ENABLED: true only on the dedicated reply worker
flags.WHATSAPP_GENERATION_ENABLED: true explicitly enables generation; absent/false does not call a model
flags.WHATSAPP_OUTBOUND_ENABLED: true explicitly enables dispatch, together with profile sendingEnabled=true and a configured token/version
flags.WHATSAPP_AUTOMATION_ENABLED: true explicitly enables automatic job creation and bot dispatch; absent/false preserves review/human operation

configuration.consistency: Use consistent profile maps and relevant generation/outbound/automation flags across the Business Manager backend, receiving worker and reply worker. All switches default off. A database migration alone does not activate external effects.

deployment: Apply migration 119 through the owner-operated Runtime migration runner after 118. No production migration was executed here.

Build Runtime so both the new migration and dist/providers/reasoning/channel-reasoner.js are packaged. Deploy backend and frontend together; deploy the new worker alongside the existing inbound worker.

Prepare and publish approved instructions, source knowledge/grants, an enabled text/voice experience with a supported published reasoning binding, and a tenant agent release through the existing Sophia Admin lifecycle. Unresolved instruction variables are not supported in this channel slice.
Extend the test-number profile and configure deployment secrets/provider settings. Keep external generation/sending/automation off until the intended test setup is approved.
Start npm run whatsapp:reply-worker with WHATSAPP_REPLY_WORKER_ENABLED=true. Generation and dispatch are separate bounded lanes; enable only the required flags.
In Company → WhatsApp configure the published agent and Draft for review first. In the inbox take ownership, request a draft and check its sources, wording and language before enabling delivery.

Use a separately authorized test-number pilot to verify real provider payloads, the callback correlation field, status reconciliation, rate limits, answer quality and actual latency. Existing Business App coexistence remains a separate verified onboarding step.

Automatic mode answers eligible new text enquiries. Existing paused or human-owned conversations require Resume Sophia. Changing reply policy puts existing bot conversations back into human attention and invalidates their undispatched jobs.

Rollback by disabling generation/outbound/automation flags and pausing receiving as appropriate. Keep records and reconcile uncertain in-flight deliveries; do not reset unknown messages to queued or blindly retry them.

operations.limits: One generation and one dispatch lane per worker process; at most two generation attempts/job and five rate-limit send attempts. No interactive request waits for a model or send. Generation lease two minutes; provider deadline 30 seconds; dispatch lease one minute; send deadline 20 seconds.
operations.retrieval: At most five excerpts of 3,000 characters; no transcript-wide or unbounded knowledge load. Source citations identify approved snapshots; citations alone do not prove factual correctness, so pilot evaluations remain required.
operations.reads: Bounded reply projection uses one scoped contact/job/outbox query plus eligibility checks, indexed by tenant/lead/time. Browser polls pending work at bounded intervals and pauses polling while hidden; no ordinary list request calls a provider.
operations.usage: Per-job measured/incomplete attempt records are retained for up to two generation attempts. This does not create a billable realtime session or claim integration with the commercial meter; confirm budget/retention/usage policy before live launch.
operations.dispatchBoundary: Cancellation protects work that has not entered dispatch. A request already in flight cannot be recalled; its accepted/uncertain result is preserved and reconciled. HTTP acceptance is shown as Sent, separately from Delivered/Read.
operations.manualRetries: Draft failures/needs-human results may be explicitly retried within the attempt bound. Response binding changes create a new revision pin. Uncertain outbound messages are not automatically retried.
operations.pilotLimits: No live provider, throughput, p95 latency, coexistence, customer-language or answer-quality evaluation was performed in this task.
operations.eligibility: Automatic generation also requires enabled sending and a current inbound reply window. Manual generation rechecks current staff authority before calling a model. Pausing or cancelling work does not recall an external request already dispatched.

verification.backend: 108 distinct backend/Runtime checks passed across targeted runs: 45 existing receiving/inbox/Settings checks, 18 new actual PostgreSQL reply tests, 4 outbound adapter tests, 3 Runtime reasoning-port tests and 38 real-estate regression tests.
verification.database: Migration 119 applied only to disposable local PostgreSQL fixtures with production-like inherited default grants. Covers takeover/newer-message races, delayed message ordering, binding revisions, bounded draft retry, source/provider retirement, current authority, explicit resume, ambiguous sends, status ordering, expired dispatch leases, concurrent dispatch and tenant/source foreign keys.
verification.browser: 52 browser checks passed at desktop 1902x1016 and mobile 390x844, including light/dark computed layout, shared controls, reply/draft separation, preserved retry identity, explicit resume, pending polling, cleanup and existing Settings/company/navigation regressions.
verification.build: Frontend TypeScript, production frontend build and Runtime build/tests passed. Existing bundle/style-budget, CommonJS and missing primeicons warnings remain.
verification.architecture: Boundary scan still reports only the two pre-existing unchanged student-document-analysis.worker.ts/spec.ts vendor imports. No new violations.
verification.external: No production database/provider calls, model requests, messages, account provisioning or deployment performed.
